title: Quantum communication: a discrimination approach
abstract: We develop a state discrimination approach to unassisted quantum communication through a noisy quantum channel. Starting from the operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, we construct entanglement-generation codes with explicit decoders constructed from Petz recovery maps. The resulting error bounds hold for every number of channel uses and are expressed in terms of Petz-Rényi coherent information. For product sources, they yield exponential error decay at rates below coherent information.
summary: This paper introduces a state discrimination framework to analyze quantum communication over noisy channels. It leverages the duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination to construct explicit coding bounds. The results provide precise, non-asymptotic estimates for the achievable error exponent, deepening the understanding of quantum channel capacity limits.
main_problem: The paper develops a state discrimination approach to analyze and establish achievable error bounds for unassisted quantum communication through a noisy quantum channel.
main_result: It derives coding bounds showing that the error in entanglement generation decays exponentially at rates related to the Petz–Rényi coherent information, holding for any number of channel uses.
method: The methodology relies on establishing an operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, utilizing explicit decoders built from Petz recovery maps.
model_or_system: The system involves quantum communication over a noisy quantum channel ($N_{A 	o B}$), aiming to reliably transfer quantum states while preserving entanglement with a reference system.
key_observables: Minimum average discrimination error ($P_{\star e}$), achievable error exponent ($\varepsilon_{EG}$), and Petz–Rényi coherent information ($I_\alpha$).
important_parameters: The number of channel uses ($n$), the dimension ($d$), and the target Schmidt rank ($d_n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is explicitly derived for product sources, although the framework is general.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the operational duality, connecting the joint measurement (packing) perspective to the recovery channel (covering) perspective.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the operational duality between entanglement recovery and state discrimination, deriving coding bounds for one-shot entanglement generation using random coding, and finally presenting strengthened hypothesis-testing bounds.
why_interesting: The connection between state discrimination and entanglement bounds provides a powerful, non-asymptotic tool for analyzing quantum channel capacity, which is fundamental to quantum information theory.
